// Generated by scripts/default-links.mjs from links.toml. Do not edit.
export const DEFAULT_LINKS_TOML: string = "# GraphOS Inspector link mappings: where a result row, or a search, opens.
#
# This is the shipped default. To add or change mappings, do not edit this
# file (an update replaces it): create ~/.claude/graphos-agent-mods/links.toml with
# only your additions, then run /gas links. Your rules come before these; your
# [bases] entries replace these.

# Named hosts. Every url below must start with one of these names in braces.
# A host comes from here or from your links.toml, with
# one exception: where `atlassian` or `slack` is left empty, an Agent Services
# response that shows your Atlassian site or Slack workspace (a URL on
# <name>.atlassian.net or <name>.slack.com) fills it. For Atlassian that is a
# Jira answer's status or priority icon (iconUrl): the `self` URLs in Agent
# Services' Jira answers go through api.atlassian.com, which names no site. Set one to a
# site, or to "" in your own links.toml to turn it off, and nothing is learned
# for it.
[bases]
atlassian = ""                # your Jira and Confluence site, e.g. https://yourco.atlassian.net; empty is learned from Agent Services' Jira answers (status and priority icons)
glean = "https://app.glean.com"
slack = ""                    # your Slack workspace, e.g. https://yourco.slack.com; empty is learned
incidentio = "https://app.incident.io"
# Hosts whose links a response carries itself (a permalink, a url, a webUrl):
# naming the host here is what lets that link open. No rule needed.
googledocs = "https://docs.google.com"
googledrive = "https://drive.google.com"
gong = "https://app.gong.io"
hubspot = "https://app.hubspot.com"
ashby = "https://app.ashbyhq.com"

# [[record]]: a result row's link. `service` is the root field's prefix before
# `_` (`*` for any), `field` the item field holding the value (dotted ok:
# fields.key), `match` an optional regex the value must fully satisfy, and
# {value} in `url` the percent-encoded value. The first rule that matches wins.
[[record]]
service = "jira"
field = "key"
match = "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+-\\d+$"
url = "{atlassian}/browse/{value}"

[[record]]
service = "jira"
field = "fields.key"
match = "^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+-\\d+$"
url = "{atlassian}/browse/{value}"

[[record]]
service = "confluence"
field = "id"
match = "^\\d{1,20}$"
url = "{atlassian}/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId={value}"

# A CQL search hit's page is under `content` (its own `url` is relative).
[[record]]
service = "confluence"
field = "content.id"
match = "^\\d{1,20}$"
url = "{atlassian}/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId={value}"

# [[search]]: a link for the whole operation, from one root's string argument.
# `root` is a root field name, or a prefix when it ends in `*`.
[[search]]
label = "Open in Confluence"
service = "confluence"
root = "confluence_*"
arg = "cql"
url = "{atlassian}/wiki/search?cql={value}"

[[search]]
label = "Open in Jira"
service = "jira"
root = "jira_*"
arg = "jql"
url = "{atlassian}/issues/?jql={value}"

[[search]]
label = "Open in Glean"
service = "glean"
root = "glean_search"
arg = "query"
url = "{glean}/search?q={value}"

# No Slack search link: its web search URL is unconfirmed, and a broken link is worse than none.
# Messages link to themselves (their permalink, on the slack host above).
"

// Emoji shortcodes drawn as the emoji they name. Pure: no $.
//
// Text from Slack, GitHub, Jira and incident.io bots carries shortcodes such
// as `:fire:` or `:large_green_circle:`; the pane shows the emoji instead.
// Only names in EMOJI are replaced. Anything else is left exactly as it came:
// a custom image Slack cannot send as text (`:slack:`), a name this table does
// not know, and text that merely looks like a shortcode (`10:30:45`,
// `std::fire::x`).
//
// Draw the result after escaping text (see escape.ts), not before: ZWJ
// sequences such as the firefighters contain U+200D (zero-width joiner), which
// escaping turns into a visible escape.

/** The longest name looked for; real names are under 40 characters. */
const NAME_MAX = 64

/** `[a-z0-9_+-]`, as Slack writes names (case-sensitive). */
const isNameChar = (code: number) =>
  (code >= 97 && code <= 122) || (code >= 48 && code <= 57) || code === 95 || code === 43 || code === 45

/** `[A-Za-z0-9_]`; NaN, past either end of the text, is not. */
const isWordChar = (code: number) =>
  (code >= 97 && code <= 122) || (code >= 65 && code <= 90) || (code >= 48 && code <= 57) || code === 95

const COLON = 58
/** `:skin-tone-2:` to `:skin-tone-6:` follow a base emoji: 2 is U+1F3FB, 6 is U+1F3FF. */
const SKIN_TONE = ':skin-tone-'
const SKIN_TONE_LENGTH = SKIN_TONE.length + 2

// Built lazily and guarded: a runtime without Unicode property escapes then
// leaves tones as their own swatch emoji instead of failing to load.
let modifiable: RegExp | null | undefined
const canTakeTone = (char: string): boolean => {
  if (modifiable === undefined) {
    try {
      modifiable = new RegExp('\\p{Emoji_Modifier_Base}', 'u')
    } catch {
      modifiable = null
    }
  }
  return modifiable !== null && modifiable.test(char)
}

/**
 * `base` with a skin tone: the modifier follows the first emoji that takes
 * one, ahead of any ZWJ (woman firefighter, medium tone: woman, tone, ZWJ,
 * fire engine), replacing U+FE0F. Null when nothing in `base` takes a tone.
 */
function withTone(base: string, tone: string): string | null {
  let at = 0
  for (const char of base) {
    at += char.length
    if (!canTakeTone(char)) continue
    const rest = base.slice(at)
    return base.slice(0, at) + tone + (rest.startsWith('\u{FE0F}') ? rest.slice(1) : rest)
  }
  return null
}

/**
 * Replaces `:name:` with its emoji when `name` is in EMOJI, and `:name::skin-tone-N:`
 * with the emoji in that tone. Linear in the length of `text`; returns `text`
 * itself when nothing changed, and never throws.
 */
export function emojify(text: string): string {
  try {
    let out = ''
    let copied = 0 // text before this index is in `out` or unchanged
    let tokenEnd = -1 // just past the last well-formed `:name:`
    let open = text.indexOf(':')
    while (open !== -1) {
      let close = open + 1
      while (close < text.length && close - open <= NAME_MAX && isNameChar(text.charCodeAt(close))) close++
      if (close === open + 1 || text.charCodeAt(close) !== COLON) {
        open = text.indexOf(':', open + 1)
        continue
      }
      // `:name:` is whole: a hit, or at least one token. A colon straight
      // after it opens the next token (`:fire::fire:`).
      const name = text.slice(open + 1, close)
      let end = close + 1
      const afterColon = open > 0 && text.charCodeAt(open - 1) === COLON && open !== tokenEnd // `a::fire::b`
      const insideWord = isWordChar(text.charCodeAt(open - 1)) && isWordChar(text.charCodeAt(end)) // `10:30:45`, `a:x:c`
      tokenEnd = end
      let emoji = !afterColon && !insideWord && Object.hasOwn(EMOJI, name) ? EMOJI[name] : undefined
      if (emoji !== undefined && text.startsWith(SKIN_TONE, end) && text.charCodeAt(end + SKIN_TONE_LENGTH - 1) === COLON) {
        const level = text.charCodeAt(end + SKIN_TONE.length) - 48
        const toned = level >= 2 && level <= 6 ? withTone(emoji, String.fromCodePoint(0x1f3fb + level - 2)) : null
        if (toned !== null) {
          emoji = toned
          end += SKIN_TONE_LENGTH
          tokenEnd = end
        }
      }
      if (emoji !== undefined) {
        out += text.slice(copied, open) + emoji
        copied = end
      }
      open = text.indexOf(':', end)
    }
    return copied === 0 ? text : out + text.slice(copied)
  } catch {
    return text
  }
}

/**
 * Shortcode name (no colons) to emoji, in emoji presentation (U+FE0F where the
 * base character would default to text). Slack's names and GitHub's both,
 * where they differ (`thumbsup` and `+1`, `large_green_circle` and
 * `green_circle`). Where they name different emoji, Slack's wins
 * (`satellite` is the satellite, `satellite_antenna` the dish).
 */
